turns.text: We have a nine-hour flight next week with our 18-month-old and I'm dreading it. What actually works to get a toddler through a long flight?
Why do toddlers struggle so much with take-off and landing? Is it the ears, and what helps?
How do I plan naps around the flight time? Should I try to keep him awake beforehand or not?
If I asked a pediatrician for tips before we go, what would they focus on?
What do experienced cabin crew say makes the biggest difference for families with toddlers?
Friends swear by a bag of small wrapped toys to unwrap one at a time. Does that hold up, and what else goes in the bag?
Another parent told me to book a bulkhead seat and ask about a bassinet. Is that worth it for an 18-month-old?
I'm so anxious about this I can't sleep. If it all goes wrong and he screams for an hour, what do I actually do?
What about food and drink on board — what should I bring for him and what usually gets past security?
Could you put together a full plan — packing list, timing, seat choice, what to do at each stage of the flight — that I can print out?
